image_description: A large, white airship (dirigible) is parked on a paved tarmac in the foreground. The airship has a long, cylindrical envelope with red and blue markings near the tail and nose. A gondola structure is visible beneath the forward section, supported by struts. Several people are standing near the nose of the airship, providing scale. In the background, there is an urban skyline with buildings, trees, and streetlights under a blue sky with scattered clouds.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with distinctive elongated oval silhouette much longer than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The aspect ratio is extremely high (length >> width), and the visible side profile suggests bilateral symmetry typical of airships.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The tail end lacks the rigid, engineered precision of a real airship. The fins seem to merge softly into the hull, and the tapering is inconsistent, suggesting a slight structural collapse or melting artifact common in AI generation.
Real airships of this size require visible propulsion systems (propellers/nacelles). Their complete absence or indistinct blending into the hull is a significant functional omission/artifact.
The struts connecting the gondola to the hull appear thin and slightly wavy, lacking the rigid, straight-line geometry expected of metal supports. They seem to 'float' or connect imprecisely.
The horizon line and building perspectives are slightly inconsistent, with some structures appearing to lean or warp subtly, though this is minor.

Presence and clarity of propulsion systems (propellers)

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tail section. AI models often struggle with the complex geometry of airship fins, resulting in melting or asymmetry. Also, verify if the lack of visible propellers is a resolution issue or a generative omission (missing functional part). Check if the gondola hangs naturally or if the struts defy gravity/physics.
